title: Free choice is not an act or habit but a faculty, belonging to man as he has intellect and will
source_text: III. Inter eos etiam constat liberum illud arbitrium quod ab homine inseparabile est, non esse actum, aut habitum aliquem, sed potius quandam animae facultatem: neque tamen isto nomine designari facultatem quandam, quae sit a mente & voluntate distincta; sed liberum arbitrium homini convenire, quatenus intellectu & voluntate praeditus est.
pass_a_gloss: Among them it is also agreed that that free choice which is inseparable from man, is not an act, or some habit, but rather a certain faculty of the soul: and yet that by that name is not designated some faculty which is distinct from mind & will; but that free choice belongs to man, inasmuch as he is endowed with intellect and will.
pass_b_english: They also agree that the free choice which cannot be separated from man is not an act or a habit. It is rather a faculty of the soul.
Even so, the name does not mean some faculty distinct from mind and will. Man has free choice because he has an intellect and a will.

choices.why: Habitus is the scholastic term for a settled disposition, as distinct from a single act or a faculty; 'habit' is the standard English term.
